ledger.contains: Prime Ministry (Petra) report of the Cabinet decision of 12 Sep 2021 amending the investor citizenship and residence bases: all routes and amounts (already recorded), holding periods, one month's presence for deposit investors, 3-year temporary passport, 4 months to hire, family inclusion (children to 18, sons to 30 over USD 3m), existing-project and partner rules, 500 investors a year, review every 6 months; the rest of the report concerns unrelated Cabinet business (15% price preference for national industry, an ambassador, the postal board), out of scope. Rules not yet recorded are added. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

English translation (4 pp., MLMUPC/ADB) of the 1996 Law on Nationality: nationality by birth and marriage (3 years), naturalisation conditions (good conduct, clean record, 7 years' residence, Khmer language and history; 3 years if born in Cambodia), exemption from residence for investors spending 1,250,000,000 riels (with or without CDC approval), donation route of 1,000,000,000 riels to the national budget, special merit, family applications (children under 18), Khmer name, Royal Decree, oath, renunciation, penalties for illegal ID or passports (5-10 years' prison). No statistics. Both amounts and the launch were already in the data; the family age rule added. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Sub-decree No. 225 on the implementation of the Law on Nationality (dated 1 Dec 2025; 19 scanned pages in Khmer, read by OCR with the khm model, annex re-read at 400 dpi). Contents: procedure and documents for claiming nationality by marriage (12 months' residence, 45/30/15 working-day review steps, appeal within 30 working days); naturalisation procedure and documents for residence, investment, donation and special-merit routes, spouses and minor children (criminal record from age 14), 45-working-day review, fee by inter-ministerial prakas (no amount), Royal Decree, oath before ID and passport; investment route: own capital of at least KHR 4,000,000,000 actually spent, in priority sectors and project types listed in the annex, plus tax compliance and an investment plan, assessed by the Ministry of Interior, lawful source of funds (Arts. 29-30); donation route: personal cash donation of at least KHR 12,000,000,000 to the national budget via the Ministry of Economy and Finance (Art. 31); renunciation (30/30/10 working days); deprivation of nationality and a 15-member national commission; repeal of Sub-decree 112 of 2018 (Art. 58); in force from signature. Annex: 12 priority sectors and project types (agriculture, agro-industry, food processing, import-substituting manufacturing, tourism, digital, high-tech/R&D, SMEs and industrial/science parks, high value-added manufacturing, regional and global value chains, SME finance, affordable housing; the last line is cut off in the scan). No statistics. Both amounts and two events were already in the data; review deadlines and the age-14 criminal record rule added. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Citizenship by Investment Unit Act, 2024 (No. 11 of 2024), 10 pages: makes the CIU a body corporate with a Board of Governors and senior officers; lists the Unit's funds (first-year appropriation; application, agent and due diligence fees; a share of post-approval-in-principle fees set by Cabinet, not above 50 percent; borrowing); sends Sustainable Island State Contributions and other statutory contributions, less agents' fees, straight to the Consolidated Fund 'as set out in the Second Schedule' (the schedule is not printed in this copy); financial year 1 July-30 June; audited accounts gazetted; annual report by 31 October; fine up to fifty thousand dollars for obstructing the auditor (not a programme number). No statistics, prices or fee amounts. Rules recorded as events: passage on 14 June 2024 (already in the data) and, new, publication on 28 June 2024 with the funding split. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

IMF press release 24/164 (15 May 2024) on the 2024 Article IV: CBI revenues 22 percent of GDP in 2023 (text, rounded; the table's 21.5 for 2023 is already recorded, so the text figure was not added as a second row for the same period), projected decline to 10 percent of GDP in 2028, advice to forgo CBI dividends and publish CBI unit reports; table of selected indicators 2019-2025 with CBI fees in percent of GDP (already recorded). Other rows are not programme numbers. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Estimates 2010, Volume I (Federal Government of St. Kitts only, EC$). Programme content: the 'Citizenship by Investment' line of non-tax revenue in the financial summary (2.1: forward estimates for 2011 and 2012, the 2010 estimate, the 2009 approved estimate, the 2008 actual) and in fiscal operations (2.2: 2010 estimate, 2009 in-year projection, 2008 actual). Revenue table R.08 (p. 71) repeats the same series in thousands under item 54-15 'Fees - Citizenship by Investment' (only CBI item; not recorded again). No expenditure programme for the CIU in this volume. Added: the 2011 and 2012 forward estimates (projection). Out of scope: all other revenue and expenditure lines; 'Fees - Certificate of Citizenship' (ordinary naturalisation) and passport fees; item 61-41 'Hurricane Relief Fund' under the Public Works/Housing (later Agriculture) revenue, which predates and is not the CBI Hurricane Relief Fund contribution; item 61-61 'Investment Proceeds' (not labelled as CBI); the salary-scale annex, which lists the posts of Director of the Citizenship by Investment Unit and Operations Manager, CIU, with general grade salaries. The year-on-year 'Increase/(Decrease)' column is not recorded (a difference of two recorded figures). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

S.R.O. 1 of 2026 (16 Jan 2026): new definition of dependant (unmarried children 18-29 substantially supported) and a replacement regulation 26 setting post approval-in-principle application fees: US$25,000 per main applicant or family of up to four, US$25,000 per additional dependant under 18, US$50,000 per additional dependant 18+, US$30,000 to add a spouse/dependant after approval-in-principle, US$7,500 per child under 3 born after citizenship; the Public Benefit fee is deducted from the US$250,000. All fee lines now recorded; event already recorded. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

S.R.O. 43 of 2024 (25 Oct 2024) amending the 2024 regulations: parent dependants from age 55 (was 65); Technical Committee membership; bankruptcy bar limited to 10 years; real estate minimum US$325,000 (was US$400,000); private real estate US$325,000 condo/share and US$600,000 single-family (were US$400,000 / US$800,000); SISC wording; appraiser rule; new US$7,500 fee for a child under 3 born after citizenship. Fee and rule-change event added; price rows already recorded. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Ministry of Justice press release (HWP, 29 Jun 2023): public-project investment immigration thresholds raised from 29 Jun 2023 (general KRW 0.5bn to 1.5bn; high-value KRW 1.5bn to 3bn), retirement scheme (55+, KRW 0.3bn) abolished; table of the three schemes with start dates (May 2013, Oct 2014); 12th investment immigration councils 14-22 June 2023 and their membership; rationale (funds lent to SMEs at low interest; no change in 10 years; PR obtainable by deposit only); foreign comparison amounts converted to won from a 2022 MOJ study (Australia, New Zealand, Portugal, US: about other countries' programmes, not recorded). Thresholds and events were already in the data; holding period, minimum age and council event added. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Ministry of Justice press release (1 May 2023): real-estate investment immigration renamed tourism and resort facility investment immigration; threshold raised to KRW 1bn; designated areas (Jeju, Incheon, Busan, Pyeongchang, Yeosu) that were to lapse on 30 Apr / 19 May 2023 extended by 3 years; 11th investment immigration councils 19-28 Apr 2023; scheme since Feb 2010 (F-2, F-5 after 5 years); plan to tighten investor permanent residence. No statistics. Threshold, launch and change events were already recorded; holding period and two events added. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Citizenship by Investment Act No. 14 of 2015 (23 pages): definitions (applicant at least 18; qualifying dependants: spouse, children under 18, children up to 25 in full-time study, disabled children, parents over 65), CBI Board of up to five members, financial year April-March, duty to publish an annual report with numbers of applications made, granted and refused (s. 24), CIU functions, application procedure, authorised agents and promoters, the Saint Lucia National Economic Fund (s. 33), due diligence, grounds for denial, review within 60 days, revocation, regulation-making powers. No programme numbers or amounts; the Senate passage (4 Aug 2015) was already recorded as an event and the assent (17 Aug 2015) is added. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Citizenship by Investment Regulations, SI 89 of 2015 (28 pages): verification, due diligence and marketing appointments, agent rules, application requirements (US$3m affidavit, police certificates from age 16, 500-a-year cap), the four qualifying investments (NEF, approved real estate held five years, enterprise projects with job creation, five-year non-interest bonds), Schedule 1 fees (agent, promoter, marketing agent, due diligence, processing, administration), Schedule 2 minimum investments by family size, Schedules 3-4 project types, Schedule 5 forms (agent licence application and certificates). All amounts are now recorded as rules (five were already present). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Citizenship by Investment (Amendment) Regulations, SI 73 of 2020 (7 pages): COVID-19 relief bond option (purchase by 31 Dec 2020; US$250,000 with 5-7 year holdings or US$300,000 for up to four dependants; US$15,000 per extra dependant; US$30,000 admin fee; processing fee waived), restated regular bond amounts, new NEF schedule (US$100,000/140,000/150,000, US$15,000 and US$25,000 per extra dependant, add-ons for families of citizens: newborn US$500, spouse US$35,000, other dependants US$25,000), certificate replacement fee US$100, admin fee waiver for real estate projects with a school. All recorded. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

SI 222 of 2022 (4 pages, in force 1 Jan 2023): due diligence fees (US$7,500 applicant, US$5,000 dependant over 16, US$7,500 per developer), certificate replacement US$500, newborn-of-citizen add-on US$5,000, real estate minimum US$200,000, bond (National Action Bond) US$300,000 for any family. All recorded (two terms and one event were already present). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

IMF 2017 Article IV staff report on St. Lucia (75 pp.). CIP content: Box 3 (p. 18) on the programme's first year (6 real estate approvals, 14 donation applications for US$1.4 million, 5 bond approvals for US$2.7 million), the 2016/17 rule changes (donation cut from US$200,000 to US$100,000, US$50,000 bond admin fee, 500 cap and US$3 million affidavit removed, US$300,000 real estate and US$1 million enterprise minimums) and the authorities' 2017/18 expectations (US$9 million donations, 80% to government, 36 real estate applications); Table 2a/2b (pp. 32-33) CIP revenue line 2013-2022 in EC$ million and % of GDP; paras 18 and 37 (risks, sovereign wealth fund plan, no numbers). The 80% transfer rule is already in events from the 2017 regulations and is not added again; the rule changes of January 2017 are already events. Rest of the report (macro, banking, debt sustainability) is out of scope. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Consolidated Lithuanian Law on the Legal Status of Aliens (IX-2206, version 1 Jul-31 Oct 2026, 143 pp.): entry, visas, temporary residence grounds (work, Blue Card with EUR 1 million company revenue condition for managers, family reunification incl. exemption for investors in state-important projects, studies, lawful activity art. 45: company participant with EUR 28,000 equity incl. EUR 14,000 own investment and wage bill of 2 average wages; EUR 260,000 investment with 5 jobs; manager of a EUR 500,000 company with 10 jobs; 1/3 shareholding; permit for 2 years; refusal/revocation if the company is fictitious or no longer meets art. 45(1)(1), (1^1), (2^2)), permanent residence, EU long-term residence, expulsion, asylum, amendment notes. Investor thresholds (14,000; 260,000) and the 2016 event were already recorded; the other art. 45 conditions and validity added. Work, Blue Card, study, family and asylum provisions are out of scope. No statistics. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Ministry of Finance FAQ (created May 2018) on the investor residence title under art. 53bis of the law of 8 March 2017 (as the FAQ names it): purpose (real-estate investments excluded), the four investment options (EUR 500,000 existing company kept 5 years; EUR 500,000 new company kept 3 years; EUR 3 million investment structure; EUR 20 million deposit kept 5 years), competent ministries, 3-year validity and annual follow-up, procedure (90-day provisional permit, derogatory procedure, arrival within 3 days, application within 3 months), criteria for the structure (2 full-time employees, 75% own funds, substance) and the deposit (100% own funds, single bank, monthly-average check), documents, forms of opinion, annual verification, renewal. The four amounts were already recorded; validity and the other numbered conditions added. No statistics. Note: the FAQ dates the law 8 March 2017, Bill 8586 says 20 March 2017. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Consolidated text of the 2002 Immigration Law on likumi.lv; only the investor provisions are in scope (art. 23(1) points 28-31, art. 23 parts on family, tax tests, renewal and payments, related rules in art. 9, 34, 35, transitional provisions); the rest is general immigration law. All prices already in program_terms; nothing new. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

All in program_terms and the 2014-09 event; nothing new. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Consolidated text of the 2002 Immigration Law on likumi.lv; only the investor provisions are in scope (art. 23(1) points 28-31, art. 23 parts on family, tax tests, renewal and payments, related rules in art. 9, 34, 35, transitional provisions); the rest is general immigration law. Consolidated text of the 2002 Immigration Law on likumi.lv; only the investor provisions are in scope (art. 23(1) points 28-31, art. 23 parts on family, tax tests, renewal and payments, related rules in art. 9, 34, 35, transitional provisions); the rest is general immigration law. Prices were already in program_terms; the suspension power and tax-debt annulment added as an event. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Consolidated text of the 2002 Immigration Law on likumi.lv; only the investor provisions are in scope (art. 23(1) points 28-31, art. 23 parts on family, tax tests, renewal and payments, related rules in art. 9, 34, 35, transitional provisions); the rest is general immigration law. All in program_terms and the 2017 event; nothing new. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Consolidated text of the 2002 Immigration Law on likumi.lv; only the investor provisions are in scope (art. 23(1) points 28-31, art. 23 parts on family, tax tests, renewal and payments, related rules in art. 9, 34, 35, transitional provisions); the rest is general immigration law. Last version of the 2002 law (20 May-14 Sep 2026): point 31 deleted by the law of 23.04.2026; otherwise investor provisions as in 2022 (wording changes only: 'meitas komersanti'); transitional provisions 16, 17, 26-33, 45, 60; list of amending laws. All in the existing events and terms; nothing new. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

New Immigration Law (adopted 20.08.2026, in force 15.09.2026). In scope: art. 27(1) p. 10 business investment (EUR 50,000/100,000 + EUR 10,000, two-year permits, tax tests), p. 36 state fund route (EUR 150,000 + EUR 10,000), art. 27(7)-(8) exclusions, art. 28 suspension power, art. 29(3) EUR 2,000 renewal payment after five years, art. 30 payments, art. 34 and 36 tax-debt refusal and annulment (EUR 150), family rules on the investor's death, transitional points 6-12 (old-law holders; EUR 1,000 per permit year for old property/bank holders). The EUR 2,000 and EUR 1,000-per-year payments were added as program terms; the rest was already in the data. Everything else is general immigration law. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

PMLP press release of 15 Sep 2026 on the new Immigration Law: end of property and bank-deposit routes, new EUR 150,000 state fund route not yet usable, two-year permit terms, language and integration rules, permanent residence changes, students' family members. The programme content is in the existing closure event and the fund-route term (from the law); no numbers beyond the EUR 150,000 already recorded. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

DOF text of the 2012 Lineamientos para trámites y procedimientos migratorios (Secretaría de Gobernación): definitions and general rules, then procedure sheets (fichas) for visas, entry, status changes, regularisation, permanent residence, documents, with fees by reference to the Ley Federal de Derechos (no amounts printed), maximum decision times and validity. In scope: the investor case for temporary residence (shareholding or business fixed assets worth 20,000 days of minimum wage, or business with at least five formal jobs; repeated in arts. 41, 43, 52), the real-estate case (40,000 days), validity (1-3 years on change of status, up to 4 years) and decision times (20 working days). The investor amount was already recorded; real estate, jobs, validity and processing time added. Economic-solvency cases (bank balances of 20,000 days or income of 400 days a month), employment offers, students and invitations are not investment routes and are not recorded. No statistics. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

European Commission North Macedonia 2025 Report (SWD(2025) 753, 105 pp.): the whole accession assessment (political criteria, economy, all chapters). Programme content is one paragraph under Chapter 23 'Citizenship rights' (PDF p. 45): the Commission's view that special-economic-interest citizenship must not be granted systematically, and grants of economic citizenship to two Turkish nationals in 2024 and one national of Bosnia and Herzegovina in 2025. Both numbers are already in the data. Other mentions of the Visa Suspension Mechanism, visa policy (Türkiye visa waiver), online citizenship certificates and FDI are not about the programme. Nothing new to add. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

European Commission screening report, Cluster 1 Fundamentals (130 pp.), covering judiciary, fundamental rights, justice/freedom/security, public procurement, statistics, financial control and public administration. Programme content (repeated on p. 68, Chapter 23 'EU citizenship rights', and p. 90, Chapter 24 visa policy): description of the investor citizenship procedure (Interior Ministry drafts, Finance and Economy ministries assess the economic interest, security agency checks, Government decides), 121 people naturalised for economic reasons 2005-2022 against 40 negative decisions, the December 2012 amendment, and the recommendation to refrain from systematic investor citizenship. All already in the data (two observations, one event). Nothing new to add. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

L.N. 167 of 2013, Global Residence Programme Rules (in force 1 Jul 2013; English text, the Maltese pages carry no extractable text): definitions, qualifying property thresholds (EUR 275,000 / 220,000 purchase; EUR 9,600 / 8,750 a year rent), application through an authorised registered mandatary with a EUR 6,000 fee (EUR 5,500 for owned property in the south), beneficiary conditions, 15% tax on remitted foreign income with a EUR 15,000 minimum, 35% on other income, cessation (incl. more than 183 days in another jurisdiction, EUR 5,000 penalty for late notification), information exchange, schedule of southern localities. Added the EUR 8,750 rent and EUR 5,500 fee; the other amounts and the start date were already recorded. The tax rates, the late-notification penalty and the 183-day rule are conditions rather than prices and are described here only. No statistics. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

L.N. 288 of 2015, Malta Residence and Visa Programme Regulations (English text): definitions (EUR 30,000 contribution incl. EUR 5,500 non-refundable fee, EUR 250,000 qualifying investment, property EUR 320,000 / 270,000 or rent EUR 12,000 / 10,000 a year), certificate rights and monitoring, application via registered agents, eligibility, conditions (property and investment held 5 years, EUR 100,000 foreign income or EUR 500,000 capital), cessation (EUR 15,000 late-notification penalty), information exchange, agent registration (agent share of the contribution capped at 10%), schedule of southern localities. All amounts except the income alternative were already recorded; added the EUR 100,000 income requirement. The penalty and the 10% agent-share ceiling are conditions, not prices, and are described here only. No statistics; the launch event is already recorded. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

L.N. 189 of 2017, MRVP (Amendment) Regulations (English text): Identity Malta replaced by the Malta Residence and Visa Agency; contribution redefined as EUR 30,000 plus EUR 5,000 per parent or grandparent; wider dependant definition; property thresholds restated (EUR 320,000 / 270,000); EUR 5,500 application fee restated; new EUR 5,000 supplementary fee for adding family members later; police certificates from age 14; Schengen-wide sickness insurance; EUR 100,000 income / EUR 500,000 capital restated; cessation grounds (b) long-term residence and (f) four years continuous stay deleted; Marsa added to southern localities. Already recorded: the EUR 5,000 parent contribution and an event for the agency change. Added: the EUR 5,000 supplementary fee and an event for the deleted cessation grounds. Restated amounts unchanged from L.N. 288 of 2015 are not repeated. No statistics. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Consolidation (posted by the agency) of S.L. 217.26, Malta Permanent Residence Programme Regulations (L.N. 121 of 2021 as amended by L.N. 57 and 310 of 2024 and 146 of 2025), 29 pages: scope and definitions (dependent children under 29, EUR 2,000 donation, property EUR 375,000, rent EUR 14,000), agent licensing by the agency (EUR 500,000 professional indemnity cover, decision within six months, licences under the old rules valid to 31 Dec 2025), application with EUR 15,000 first fee instalment, capital EUR 500,000 (EUR 150,000 financial) or EUR 650,000 (EUR 75,000 financial), payment deadlines (two and eight months from approval in principle), rights, dependants and later additions, eligibility and due diligence, conditions (property five years then a residential property; capital five years), cessation, data protection, confidentiality, agent payments, MRVP transition (29 Mar 2021, 24-month bar), First Schedule (EUR 60,000 fee, EUR 7,500 per dependant other than spouse, minor or disabled child, EUR 37,000 contribution), Second Schedule repealed, Third Schedule (EUR 5,000 annual agent licence fee). Every amount and the MPRP launch event are already recorded from L.N. 121 of 2021, 310 of 2024 and 146 of 2025 (and the launch event from this document). L.N. 57 of 2024 is marked against regs 15, 17 and 21 (conditions, cessation, confidentiality) but the consolidation does not show what it changed and prints no amounts or dates for it, so no event is added. The EUR 500,000 indemnity cover is an agent condition, described here only. No statistics. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Government Decision of 30 Dec 2021 amending the programme decision (Službeni list CG 143/2021, 2 image-only pages): innovation added to the purpose; agent licences renewable three times instead of twice; new EUR 100,000 escrow payment for the Innovation Fund; listed tourism projects need a first-demand bank guarantee of 50% of the minimum investment, to be delivered within 30 days or the project is struck off; new list of documents; escrow transfer covers the new payment; programme extended to 31 Dec 2022; in force on publication. Innovation Fund term and the extension event were already in the dataset; this pass adds the guarantee terms and the licence-renewal event. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Government Decision of 30 Jun 2023 (Službeni list CG 67/2023, 1 image-only page) adding art. 5e to the general decision on criteria for citizenship in the interest of Montenegro: licences of intermediary and due-diligence agents stay valid until decisions on all programme applications filed by 31 Dec 2022; in force on publication. No figures besides dates and gazette numbers; the rule is already recorded as an event. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Government Decision of 23 Jun 2022 amending the programme decision (Službeni list CG 68/2022, 1 image-only page): project bank guarantee changed from 50% of the minimum investment to EUR 1,000,000; ministry name changed; children born after the application during the programme count as family members, with an application fee of EUR 50,000 per such child; investors may replace their guarantee within 45 days to get the old one returned; in force on publication.
